query: Which method can be used for oxidation resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Stationary friction processing improves the oxidation resistance of AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys by refining the grain structure, thereby promoting the formation of protective oxide layers.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast equimolar AlCoCrFeNi HEA with coarse grain structure (~98 μm) that tends to form nonprotective spinel oxides during oxidation.
generation.intervention: Application of stationary friction processing at high rotational speeds (e.g., 400 rpm and 1800 rpm for 5 minutes) to achieve an ultrafine-grain microstructure.
generation.conditions: Isothermal oxidation in laboratory air at temperatures between 850 °C and 1050 °C for a duration of 100 hours.
generation.structural_mediator: The creation of an ultrafine-grained microstructure with high grain boundary density and a phase transformation (increased FCC fraction) compared to the as-cast state.
generation.mechanism: The increased grain boundary area accelerates the outward diffusion of Cr ions, facilitating the formation of a dense, protective Cr2O3 layer (along with Al2O3 formation via inward oxygen diffusion) while the higher surface free energy suppresses the formation of nonprotective spinel oxides.
generation.predicted_outcome: A marked reduction in oxidation kinetics (lower mass gain and parabolic rate constants) compared to the as-cast material, with the sample processed at higher rotational speed (1800 rpm) showing the greatest improvement.
generation.baseline: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi HEA which shows larger grain sizes, formation of nonprotective spinels, and faster oxidation kinetics at the tested temperatures.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is specific to equimolar AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys processed by stationary friction processing and evaluated under high-temperature oxidation in air; outcomes may vary with different alloy systems or processing conditions.
generation.uncertainty: Quantitative differences in oxidation rate reduction and the relative contributions of grain boundary diffusion versus phase transformation across different temperatures remain uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of AlCoCrFeNi HEA samples, one as-cast and one processed via stationary friction processing at varying rotational speeds (including 400 and 1800 rpm). Expose all samples to isothermal oxidation in laboratory air at predetermined temperatures (850, 950, and 1050 °C) for 100 hours.
measurements: Grain size and phase distribution using SEM/TEM and XRD
Mass gain over time to determine oxidation kinetics
Parabolic rate constant (k_p) calculations from oxidation data
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the processed samples do not exhibit significantly reduced mass gain and lower parabolic oxidation rate constants in comparison to the as-cast samples, or if no substantial grain refinement and protective oxide layer formation are confirmed, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Paper card. Question: How does an ultrafine-grain microstructure, obtained via stationary friction processing, affect the oxidation behavior of AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy?. System: Equimolar AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy (HEA). Processing: Stationary friction processing (SFP) using a WC-cylindrical tool (12 mm diameter) at rotational speeds of 400 rpm and 1800 rpm for 5 min duration. Test conditions: Isothermal oxidation in laboratory air at 850, 950, and 1050 °C for 100 h. Findings: Grain size refined from 98 μm (as-cast) to 1 μm (SFP_400) and 0.43 μm (SFP_1800).; Phase transformation from BCC/B2 to FCC occurred, with 38% and 55% FCC fraction for SFP_400 and SFP_1800, respectively.; Surface free energy increased by 29.8% for SFP_400 and 35.2% for SFP_1800 compared to as-cast.; Oxidation kinetics decelerated by 12–20% for SFP_400 and 38–48% for SFP_1800 compared to as-cast.; Cumulative mass gain at 850 °C after 100 h was 0.33 mg/cm² (as-cast), 0.27 mg/cm² (SFP_400), and 0.17 mg/cm² (SFP_1800).; Parabolic rate constants (k_p) at 1050 °C were 23.2 × 10⁻¹³ g²·cm⁻⁴·s⁻¹ (as-cast), 18.4 × 10⁻¹³ (SFP_400), and 8.16 × 10⁻¹³ (SFP_1800).; Processed samples formed predominantly protective
